key_insight: LLM-enhanced frailty assessment identified more hospitalizations as frail but did not significantly improve prognostic discrimination over a standard electronic frailty index.
clinical_relevance: Adding functional deficits from physical therapy notes increased sensitivity for adverse outcomes, but reduced specificity.
method: Retrospective cohort of 616 hospitalizations among adults aged ≥50 years at two affiliated hospitals.
Compared a validated 35-deficit electronic frailty index with an enhanced index incorporating GPT-4o-extracted deficits from physical therapy notes.
Evaluated associations and discrimination for discharge to a facility, readmission, or death within 90 days.
evidence_signal: Frailty classification increased from 35.1% to 58.8%, while AUROC changed from 0.636 to 0.660 without a statistically significant difference (p=0.12); sensitivity rose from 42.5% to 69.4%, and specificity fell from 73.0% to 52.7%.
watch_item: Physical therapy documentation was available for only 53.4% of hospitalizations, potentially limiting consistency of LLM-based enhancement across patients.
paper_title: Large Language Model-Enhanced Electronic Frailty Assessment and Prognostic Performance in Hospitalized Adults: A Retrospective Cohort Study
